# RUNE patch of openmls_rust_crypto 0.5.1

RUNE uses this copy through `[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace `Cargo.toml`.
It reaches the build as `davey 0.1.5` -> `openmls_rust_crypto ^0.5.1` (DAVE's
MLS crypto provider), and as a dev-dependency of `rune-discord-session` (the
synthetic voice server's MLS fixtures). See `vendor/davey/RUNE-PATCH.md` for
why: the 0.5.1 release needs `p256 0.13` and `hpke-rs-rust-crypto 0.6`, both
on `elliptic-curve 0.13` -> `crypto-bigint 0.5.5` (RUSTSEC-2026-0387).

## Source

- Archive: `https://static.crates.io/crates/openmls_rust_crypto/openmls_rust_crypto-0.5.1.crate`
- SHA-256: `fafcc8a3552b10fbb3ab757cccaf1a34081e826ca819f49aa7e6645b1d95c00f`,
  identical to the crates.io checksum recorded in RUNE's `Cargo.lock` before
  the patch.
- Upstream commit (`.cargo_vcs_info.json`):
  `47dbedecad0c1fd8eb5368d582250ebfcc1e1ce6` of `openmls/openmls`, path
  `openmls_rust_crypto`.
- License: MIT (declared in `Cargo.toml`). The archive ships no license text,
  so `LICENSE` is the repository's own file at that commit
  (SHA-256 `43e5e3c4b5cca67f9ea912f7e1929702a848aa765d3b3e14f25d3838a5a5565d`).

Every other file is the archive content unchanged, except the archive's own
`Cargo.lock`, removed. `Cargo.toml.orig` and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` stay as
provenance.

## Changes

The edits follow, call for call, what upstream openmls `main` did in the same
file (`be248d4b1306d87a641ce24ed0ffcab2b27967f6`, unreleased as
`openmls_rust_crypto 0.6.0`) when it moved to `p256 0.14` and `hpke-rs 0.8`;
upstream's other changes (P-384, ML-DSA, PSK, new `openmls_traits` API) are
not taken, so the crate still implements `openmls_traits 0.5` for openmls 0.8.

1. `Cargo.toml`: `p256 "0.13"` -> `"0.14"`; `hpke-rs`, `hpke-rs-crypto` and
   `hpke-rs-rust-crypto` `"0.6.0"` -> `"0.8"`; `rand "0.8"` replaced by
   `rand_core "0.10"` and `getrandom "0.4"` (feature `sys_rng`);
   `rand_chacha "0.3"` -> `"0.10"`; `ed25519-dalek "2.0"` -> `"3.0"` (its
   key generation takes the `rand_core 0.10` RNG). `sha2`, `aes-gcm`,
   `chacha20poly1305`, `hkdf` and `hmac` keep their versions.
2. `src/provider.rs`:
   - the provider's `ChaCha20Rng` is seeded with
     `from_rng(&mut UnwrapErr(SysRng))` instead of `from_entropy()` (both the
     operating system's RNG);
   - P-256 key generation: `SigningKey::random` -> `generate_from_rng` on the
     same RNG, `to_encoded_point(false)` -> `to_sec1_point(false)`;
   - P-256 verification: `VerifyingKey::from_encoded_point(EncodedPoint::from_bytes(pk))`
     -> `VerifyingKey::from_sec1_bytes(pk)`;
   - P-256 signing: the private key slice is converted with `try_into()`, so
     a key of the wrong length returns `CryptoError::InvalidLength` instead
     of panicking.

The HPKE calls compile unchanged against `hpke-rs 0.8` (upstream left them
as they were too). No algorithm, encoding or wire-format change: ECDSA
P-256/SHA-256 signatures stay DER, public keys uncompressed SEC1, and HPKE
DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) with AES-128-GCM is RFC 9180 either way.

## Validation

- RUNE: `cargo test --workspace`, including the DAVE tests of
  `rune-discord-session` against the synthetic voice server, whose MLS
  external sender and members use this provider.
- Interop, in a scratch crate outside the workspace linking this copy and
  the crates.io `openmls_rust_crypto 0.5.1` / `openmls_basic_credential
  0.5.0` side by side, for the `MLS_128_DHKEMP256_AES128GCM_SHA256_P256`
  primitives: P-256 keys generated by each side signed by the other and
  verified by both (and rejected for another message); identical HPKE key
  pairs derived from the same IKM; HPKE seal on one side and open on the
  other in both directions (rejected with a wrong AAD); identical HPKE
  exporter secrets from sender on one side and receiver on the other.

## When to remove

Drop this directory and its `[patch.crates-io]` entry together with
`vendor/davey` (see there).
